name: Ewam Garden of One Thousand Buddhas
tradition: Nyingma School of Tibetan Buddhism — a public Buddhist garden and retreat/study center under Gochen Tulku Sang-ngag Rinpoche
teacherAccess: Multi-day retreats, ceremonies, and Shedra courses are taught directly by Gochen Tulku Sang-ngag Rinpoche and resident/visiting Tibetan and Western teachers, with group instruction, individual practice guidance, and periodic personal interviews.
retreatOptions: Multi-day residential programs held on-site, including the 12-day annual Ewam Buddhist Institute (Shedra) study courses each held in July, the roughly 9-day Sangwa Yeshe Drubchöd group practice ceremony, and the annual month-long Yangti Gomde retreat cycle (progressive levels held August into September) for continuing students.
about: The Ewam Garden of One Thousand Buddhas is a public park, botanical garden, and Tibetan Buddhist center in Montana's Jocko Valley near Arlee, on land of the Confederated Salish and Kootenai Tribes. Founded by Gochen Tulku Sang-ngag Rinpoche of the Nyingma School, the Garden is both a free public pilgrimage site and the home of the Ewam Buddhist Institute (Shedra), which teaches multi-day residential courses on the complete Buddhist path each summer, and of the annual Yangti Gomde, a roughly month-long gathering where continuing students progress through ngondro, deity practice, and Dzogchen training under Rinpoche's guidance. Retreatants can stay on-site in camping, shared-room, or single-room accommodations. The Garden also hosts a large annual group ceremony (the Sangwa Yeshe Drubchöd) and free community events such as the Peace Festival, though those day events are separate from its residential retreat and study programs.
technique: Tibetan Vajrayana meditation including ngondro (preliminary practices), deity yoga (kyerim), subtle-body practices (tsalung, including tummo and trulkhor), and progressive Dzogchen meditation within the Yangti Nagpo cycle.
schedule: Residential program days combine two teaching/practice sessions with study or contemplation; ceremonial retreats center on daily group ritual practice (drupchö) in front of the Garden's central Yum Chenmo statue; the public garden itself keeps separate seasonal daily visiting hours.
cost: Specific current per-night or per-retreat pricing is not published on the official retreat/program pages checked; residential participants in multi-day programs are housed on-site (camping, shared, or single rooms) for the duration of the course.
foodNotes: Residential program participants are housed and fed on-site for the duration of multi-day courses and retreats; specific meal/diet details were not published on the pages checked.
workNotes: Paid, room-and-board internships (e.g. Garden Helper, Gift Shop Clerk) are advertised separately from the retreat/study programs; no work requirement is stated for retreat or Shedra participants themselves.
